project.title: Q-CoMem: Quantized Split Replay for Memory-Constrained Hybrid LLMs
project.paper_identity: A capacity-first extension of CoMem split replay for hybrid LLMs on one fixed Qwen3.5/H20 stack: quantize the complete retained hybrid split-replay entry (boundary residual plus lower-layer KV and convolution/recurrent state) to reduce retained per-document Store, at an explicit and measured TTFT cost and bounded measured F1 change. ForkAudit is the subordinate correctness component that validates the immutable-document / request-local-mutable ownership boundary with storage evidence rather than output equality. The paper claims neither lower total VRAM, nor measured Recall, nor edge-hardware performance, nor faster inference.

A fresh run independently reproduces the archival -0.4455 [-2.059, 0.991]. T-02 closed by printing the BF16-normalised column including the 28.683 MiB value the paper had never printed, plus a new Appendix C carrying the group-quantization byte identity and the per-component table. The ninth ForkAudit scope site was added in the Introduction. Residency was deliberately omitted entirely, because capacity_estimate divides a measured budget by the measured per-document payload and reporting it beside the Store ratio would present one measurement as two. Latency concession strengthened: dense-prefill-once reaches the first token sooner than Q-CoMem on 60 items. Build clean, main text ends page 9, independently rebuilt. PANEL: unanimous 4, zero dispersion, medians 2/2/2, 4 critical / 29 major, meta-score 4. Flat against R44's unanimous 4 despite eight integrated actions; criticals fell 6 to 4. The meta-review overturned REV-1's Q8-defect allegation and REV-2's concurrency bound, and confirmed REV-4's bit-width confound, which cancels to the same number by a different route. AUTHOR-SIDE CORRECTION: the A16 reading that frozen j=7 beats the strongest quantized exact cache by 5.84x was width-confounded and was written into the abstract, introduction, Sections 5.2 and 5.4 and the conclusion; the meta-review rebuilds it exactly as 3.9174x split times 1.4912x width, so the split-attributable factor is 3.918x and the manuscript overstates it.
